correctness.rationale: The general dichotomy is an immediate consequence of the unique normalized duality map for 1<p<infinity and unconstrained complex scalar multiplication in mul(T). The non-even projective independence lemma is proved by isolating a single vanishing complex-linear form while others stay nonzero, so nonanalytic signed-power behavior cannot cancel an analytic germ. Dimension-one and zero-coordinate cases are explicitly handled. For p=2j, monomial independence gives the exact finite coefficient matrix nullspace; its rank is invariant under changing a basis of D. The binomial family follows from the order-2k finite-difference identity and strict positivity of the 2k-th derivative for larger even exponents. All-order reasoning is analytic; the checker replay verifies only finite samples.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 theory offers a finite-domain dichotomy but leaves undecided exactly which multivalued parts preserve bounded numerical range. This result solves that decision problem for every finite-dimensional complex ell_p space, computes the maximal allowable multivalued dimension directly from D at all exponents, and exhibits an arbitrarily long prescribed finite list of even p-values for which a fixed nontrivial relation collapses from the entire complex plane to a singleton. The explicit all-spectrum example illustrates why the adjoint in the spectral-inclusion theorem matters. The object and invariant are natural; the finite-difference construction is a sharp boundary witness, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff.
